restart_and_interruption.owner_call_actually_invoked: TWO SEPARATE OS PROCESSES. Process A: BatchExecutionRunner.run(max_units=5) then the harness serializes receipts via UnitExecutionReceipt.projection(). Process B (independent interpreter, handed only the file): UnitExecutionReceipt rehydration from those projections, then BatchExecutionRunner(prior_receipts=...).run()
restart_and_interruption.expectation: execution progress survives genuine process loss when receipts are serialized
restart_and_interruption.observed: procA: completed=5/10 state=IN_PROGRESS; procB: restored=5, final=10/10, full=True
restart_and_interruption.critical_caveat: This passes ONLY because the CALLER serialized the receipts. The owner contributed no persistence. See B01-P04 and F-01.

restart_and_interruption.owner_call_actually_invoked: BatchExecutionRunner constructed with NO prior_receipts after the caller's serialized receipt file was deleted, then run to completion
restart_and_interruption.expectation: with no recovery input the owner redoes all work at-least-once and never reports false completion
restart_and_interruption.observed: no-input start: completed=0/10 state=READY pending=10; after re-run: completed=10/10 full=True; manifest identity unchanged
restart_and_interruption.significance: Correct and safe, but it means the entire unit set is recomputed after total process loss. There is no partial-progress store to consult.

restart_and_interruption.expectation: an interrupted adaptive search survives a REAL disk round-trip and resumes to exactly the one-shot result identity
restart_and_interruption.observed: partial_state=PARTIAL_INTERRUPTED unvisited=2; checkpoint_bytes=7111; disk_roundtrip_identity_stable=True; one-shot checkpoint ref == resumed-from-disk checkpoint ref
restart_and_interruption.significance: The I05 adaptive checkpoint IS genuinely serializable and IS identity-stable across a real disk round-trip. This is the strongest restart-grade result measured in this commission.

cancellation.expectation: owner-level cooperative stop via max_units leaves typed pending coverage
cancellation.scope_limit: max_units is a COOPERATIVE THROTTLE applied between whole units. It is not a mid-unit abort, not a signal handler and not a timeout mechanism. No owner API exists to cancel a unit already inside an executor call.

cancellation.note: No cancel/abort/timeout/signal API exists on BatchExecutionRunner, BatchUnitSpec, ExecutorBinding, execute_route_b_production or bounded_empirical_runtime. A host that loses its process loses the in-flight unit. This is an ABSENCE OF OWNER OPERATION, not a test that failed.

duplicate_publication_prevention.area: duplicate publication at the PRODUCT layer
duplicate_publication_prevention.expectation: an idempotent publish/commit boundary that refuses a second publication of the same semantic result
duplicate_publication_prevention.note: BatchExecutionRunner owns EXECUTION receipts only. It has no product commit/publication step, so no duplicate-publication hostile can be executed against it. The nearest owner-side atomic swap is C11Repository._commit_validated (in-memory). Publication-layer idempotency belongs to C02 scope, not B01.

checkpoint_tamper_and_staleness.observed: identity_changed=True; visited_set_equal_to_one_shot=True; duplicate_units=False; terminal completeness equal (both EXPLORATORY_POLICY_FRONTIER_EXHAUSTED); checkpoint_identity_converges=False. one_shot order ['b01-root','b01-child','b01-later'] vs resumed order ['b01-child','b01-root','b01-later']
checkpoint_tamper_and_staleness.finding: CHECKPOINT_IDENTITY_IS_VISIT_ORDER_SENSITIVE. A rewritten checkpoint re-executes an EQUAL work set and reaches the EQUAL terminal state, but produces a DIFFERENT checkpoint ref purely because visit ordering differs. Safety holds (no skipped work, no duplicate unit, no false completion); identity determinism does not converge.
checkpoint_tamper_and_staleness.honest_limitation: AdaptiveSearchCheckpoint.from_dict does NOT reject the tampered dict. Detection is only available to a caller that independently compares the content-addressed ref. There is no owner-side tamper rejection path.

protocol_mandate_without_implementation.observation: rawlsing_next/rabochii_execution_protocol.py:300-323 REQUIRES, for REAL_EXECUTION profiles, a checkpoint_state with mode WRITE_AHEAD and, while a volatile result is pending, a PERSIST_CHECKPOINT action. It also forbids volatile_result_pending coexisting with durable_checkpoint_ref.
protocol_mandate_without_implementation.evidence: A repository-wide search for PERSIST_CHECKPOINT, durable_checkpoint_ref and checkpoint_state matches only this validator and its test file. No owner code creates a durable checkpoint.
protocol_mandate_without_implementation.consequence: The written protocol mandates a write-ahead durable checkpoint that the codebase does not implement. Any REAL_EXECUTION claim would be running ahead of the implemented capability. This is a documentation-vs-implementation gap, not an executed failure.
